investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 125–151 seconds across all three checks, exhausting the eval timeout before any VM was assigned, which means no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the two eligible nodes. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-18T03:23–03:30Z), both kata-capable nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption found no victims, meaning all available VM slots were occupied by existing workloads. The 4 remaining nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so scheduling was impossible. Because the pod never became schedulable, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a running VM, and the eval timed out without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

The two kata-capable nodes may have been temporarily degraded, cordoned, or under memory/CPU pressure, causing the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to report as insufficient even if nominal capacity exists.

The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod template may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run kata peer-pods, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 of 6 nodes.

A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) may have saturated the kata VM pool at the moment the eval ran, causing a transient but complete capacity exhaustion.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available for scheduling — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval checks in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

No agent pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity (no preemption victims available), and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) timed out after ~125–151 seconds without returning any evidence, causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pods. No preemption victims were found, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes.

Tertiary: Cluster under-provisioning — the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workload, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability: A recent change to pod affinity rules or resource requests in the agent pod spec (not evidenced in the supplied source artifacts) could have tightened scheduling constraints, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 125–151 seconds across all three checks, exhausting the eval timeout before any VM was assigned, which means no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the two eligible nodes. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-18T03:23–03:30Z), both kata-capable nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption found no victims, meaning all available VM slots were occupied by existing workloads. The 4 remaining nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so scheduling was impossible. Because the pod never became schedulable, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a running VM, and the eval timed out without writing any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

The two kata-capable nodes may have been temporarily degraded, cordoned, or under memory/CPU pressure, causing the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource to report as insufficient even if nominal capacity exists.

The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod template may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run kata peer-pods, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 of 6 nodes.

A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) may have saturated the kata VM pool at the moment the eval ran, causing a transient but complete capacity exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No agent pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity (no preemption victims available), and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) timed out after ~125–151 seconds without returning any evidence, causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — existing remote-agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pods. No preemption victims were found, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-saturated nodes.

Tertiary: Cluster under-provisioning — the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workload, causing contention during the eval window.

Lower probability: A recent change to pod affinity rules or resource requests in the agent pod spec (not evidenced in the supplied source artifacts) could have tightened scheduling constraints, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
